title: Diagnose a failed SDDC Manager credential rotation from logs and events
prompt:
Our scheduled overnight ESXi password rotation failed on our VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 fleet. SDDC Manager only tells us "Password rotation completed with failures for one or more resources", which nobody can act on, and I am not having another engineer click through the UI at 02:00 to work out what happened.

Read docs/incident.md - that is ticket SDDC-51782 - and implement src/VcfDiagnostics.java so it runs the investigation against SDDC Manager and writes out/diagnosis.json in the shape the ticket specifies.

Before implementing, research `createToken`, `getTasks`, `getCredentialsTask`, `getCredentialsSubTask`, `getNotifications`, `startSupportBundle`, and `getSupportBundleStatus` in `specifications/sddc-manager/sddc-manager-openapi.json` from VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at tag `9.0.0.0`. Confirm their methods, paths, authentication, parameters, request and response schemas, status codes, and status vocabularies, and cite the exact specification URLs you consulted in your final answer. Use only those seven operations. Do not send properties or query parameters absent from the 9.0 schemas, and omit optional properties with no value rather than sending null or empty strings.

Do not guess the cause from the top-level task; it is generic, and so is the subtask roster. The evidence is in the per-subtask detail and in the system notifications SDDC Manager raised around the failure, lined up against each other. Several unrelated warnings landed in the same window and one of them is the same kind of warning about a different domain, so correlate rather than taking the first plausible hit.

Keep the client in that one file using only the JDK standard library. Run `./run_tests.sh`. Verification checks evidence correlation across task, subtask, and notification data; exact request shapes; support-bundle collection; and the report required by `docs/incident.md`. Change only `src/VcfDiagnostics.java`.

workspace.description: Contents of files/ are laid out as the project root the task runs in.

verification.description: Starts the loopback mock, compiles VcfDiagnostics with TestMain, runs the harness, then runs verify/verify.py over the mock's recorded request log and out/diagnosis.json. 73 assertions covering the exact request wire shape and the diagnosis content.

network.notes: The mock binds 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port. No VMware endpoint is contacted at any point, by the task or by the verifier.
